- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast peak values by 5–15%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” bias: reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment alternates sharply (e.g., +1 then -1), model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing 3-day moving average.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is positive and recent price is trending upward; increase forecast by 3–8% for 2–4 days if sentiment >0 and price > previous 5-day high.
- If true outcome is significantly lower than forecast (e.g., >10% gap), check if sentiment was positive 3–5 days prior — if so, apply “mean reversion” correction: reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5 days.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to over-forecast; apply 5–10% downward adjustment if true outcome is below 85% of forecast mean.
